argument_summary: The certification request should be read narrowly. The admissible record supports the business judgment to certify on a caveated basis because the release clears aggregate readiness and showed no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and the governing public guidance supports documented limitations plus post-deployment monitoring. The same record also shows a current developer-support migration weakness and does not support an unconditional finding that present documentation already satisfies the release-policy predicate. The supportable position is therefore certification only as caveated compliance: the release is certifiable if, and only if, the current release documentation is updated to reflect the current evaluation result and explicitly disclose that named subgroup weakness, or equivalent approved risk acceptance exists for this release.
claims_about_business_cost: Business-cost considerations are not the basis for the compliance position and should not control the verdict. The admissible case stands or falls on whether certification is treated as caveated and documentation-bound under policy.
claims_about_policy: Policy does not make aggregate readiness and clean rehearsal results sufficient on their own. It requires current release documentation to reflect current evaluation results and requires material segment weaknesses for named launch use cases to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved mitigation. On the present admissible record, prior approval and informal monitoring can be treated as contextual support for a monitored launch posture, but not as substitutes for current disclosure or release-specific approval. That means the certification case is not clean unconditional compliance; it is supportable only as caveated compliance tied to current documentation.
concessions: The current record does not prove that the current release model card or release documentation already reflects the developer-support migration regression.
The current record does not show approved mitigation or formal risk acceptance for this exact release.
Prior approval from four months ago and an informal monitoring comment do not independently satisfy the current policy requirements.
